facts.raw_span: 2 months of progressive right earache and headache without fever
without fever
2 weeks of mild left-sided weakness
1 week of intermittent hallucinations and nonsensical speech
left pronator drift
no obvious manifestation of external ear canal infection during endoscopy of the right ear
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 42 mm/h (normal, <20 mm/h)
C-reactive protein level: 25 mg/L (normal, <10 mg/L)
Glycosylated hemoglobin A1C level: 6.8% (normal, 4.3%-6.1%)
positive for anti-NMDAR antibodies (CSF titer 1:320, serum titer 1:100)
CT scan of temporal bone showed otitis media, mastoiditis, and local bone destruction in the right ear
Coronal FLAIR image demonstrated extensive area of hyperintensity with compressed right lateral ventricle

concepts.why: The presence of anti-NMDAR antibodies in the CSF and serum, along with symptoms such as hallucinations and nonsensical speech, supports this diagnosis.
The CT scan showing otitis media and the patient's symptoms of earache support this diagnosis.
The CT scan showing mastoiditis and the patient's symptoms of earache support this diagnosis.
The patient's glycosylated hemoglobin A1C level is elevated, indicating this diagnosis.
The presence of Candida tropicalis in the CSF and the patient's symptoms of headache and confusion support this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: Progressive earache and headache without fever suggests an inflammatory process, possibly related to otitis media or mastoiditis, but also consistent with anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
rationales.F04: Intermittent hallucinations and nonsensical speech are highly suggestive of anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
rationales.F09: Elevated Glycosylated hemoglobin A1C level indicates poor glucose control, consistent with type 2 diabetes.
rationales.F10: Presence of anti-NMDAR antibodies is highly specific for anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
rationales.F11: CT scan findings of otitis media, mastoiditis, and local bone destruction are consistent with these conditions.
